mechanism.name: factorized Euclidean-hyperbolic joint codebook
mechanism.question: Can one 32-dimensional joint code per level be factorized into an E16 branch codebook and an H16 branch codebook, with the 256 branch pairs assigned jointly, so the token count and capacity stay the same and both geometries are expressed independently?
mechanism.one_sentence: Each level keeps 256 joint codes, but they are the pairs of two 16-code branch codebooks; the joint cost is the sum of the branch costs, the assignment is the baseline's Sinkhorn over the expanded 256 candidates, and the token is the packed pair 16*k_E + k_H.
mechanism.distinct_from: The frozen mixed tree stores 256 independent 32-d codes; here the 256 codes are a 16 x 16 product, so the two branch marginals can be balanced independently while the joint pair still decides the token.

computations.statement: Level codeword = (k_E, k_H), k_E, k_H in [0, 16); token = 16*k_E + k_H. The packing is a bijection [0,16)^2 -> [0,256). Three levels still export three tokens.
C(i, k_E, k_H) = ||rE_i - eE_{k_E}||^2 + d_c(rH_i, exp_0(eH_{k_H}))^2 / 4, evaluated for all 256 pairs; c = 1 is frozen.

Nearest joint pair on levels 1 and 2, the baseline's balanced Sinkhorn over the expanded 256 candidates on level 3 during training, deterministic nearest pair at export. The two branches are never selected separately.
rE' = rE - eE_{k_E}; rH' = project((-exp_0(eH_{k_H})) (+) rH). The chosen branch codes are detached.
Rank-zero KMeans of the E residual into 16 E centers and of log_0 of the H residual into 16 H centers, broadcast to every rank.

The exported token of each level IS the joint pair index, so the per-level token usage reported by the layer record and the structural report is the joint-pair usage; branch marginals can be read by unpacking the same tokens.

inputs.graph: the canonical TRAIN behaviour graph, read only after export for the external AF3 evaluation

outputs.sid: three packed-pair tokens per item plus the disambiguation token
outputs.branch_usage: per-level joint-pair usage, plus E and H marginals by unpacking

learned: three E branch codebooks of 16 x 16
three H branch codebooks of 16 x 16

gradient_rules.branch_codebooks: the selected E branch code and the selected H branch code each receive the commitment and codebook terms of their own branch cost
gradient_rules.residual: the chosen branch codes are detached

training_integration.records: logs/training_metrics.jsonl records one train event per epoch; pair usage is measured on the exported tokens

conventions.distance: d_0(x, y) = 2||x - y||; d_c(x, y) = 2 atanh(sqrt(c)||(-x) (+) y||)/sqrt(c)
conventions.token: one packed joint pair per level, values in [0, 256)

switches.GEOMETRY_ON: the factorized E16 x H16 joint codebook
switches.GEOMETRY_OFF: a single un-factorized 256-code Euclidean level; only a cheap wiring check, never trained
switches.BEHAVIOUR_ON: not applicable: AF3 never enters forward, loss, sampling or gradients in this issue
switches.policy: no arm with a switch off is trained

excluded.surface: the packing and the pair expansion
the assignment and the Sinkhorn balancing
excluded.reason: discrete; the rule is the baseline's
plain squared Euclidean distance, the frozen baseline's surface

excluded.surface: the 32-dimensional norm inside the H branch cost
excluded.reason: the contract states the width-1 surface; the callable applies it to the norm

continuous_surface.note: The width-1 form of the H branch cost d_c(r, exp_0(q))^2/4 at c = 1. The trained implementation applies the same expression to the norm of the 16-d branch; the norm form is excluded and covered by tests/test_math.py.
